note: near-identity: c = 1/12 + Pi^2/(6 ln^2 2) - alpha - beta (Finch), alpha + beta = sum sigma(n)/2^n is the Eisenstein series E2 at q = 1/2, and its quasi-modular transformation gives c = 1/ln 4 + 1/24 + (4 Pi^2/ln^2 2) sum sigma(n) exp(-4 Pi^2 n/ln 2); the first correction is 1.5e-23, so 1/ln 4 + 1/24 alone agrees to 22.7 digits (found by the engine at K = 7); checked to 100 digits with mpmath
